thread.title: Livingston County appoints Matthew Lenahan as new county attorney
thread.title_full: Livingston County appoints Matthew Lenahan as new county attorney

author: k. n. salazar
title: Livingston County appoints Matthew Lenahan as new county attorney
text:
Matthew Lenahan has been appointed as the new county attorney for Livingston County, following a decision by the board of supervisors during their regular meeting on May 13. Lenahan will begin his role on June 29.
The appointment is significant for Livingston County as it brings an experienced legal professional to serve as the primary legal advisor to the board of supervisors and other county officials. With more than two decades of experience in law, Lenahan has worked extensively with municipal entities and has previously served as village attorney for Lima and Honeoye Falls.
“Matt’s experience with municipal law and his track record of providing sound counsel to local villages made him the ideal choice for this role,” said Board Chair David LeFeber. “We look forward to working alongside him to navigate the legal landscape of local government.”
County Administrator Shannon Hillier, who held the position of county attorney from 2017 to 2025 before becoming administrator, also spoke about Lenahan’s qualifications. “Matt brings exceptional legal experience, sound judgment, and professional expertise to this key County position,” said Hillier. “The board and I are confident his leadership will strengthen our operations and support the board and County staff in advancing our goals. We look forward to the positive impact Matt will make in this important role.”
Lenahan expressed enthusiasm about joining Livingston County government: “I was drawn to the opportunity to serve in a public role at the county level and to work on issues that directly affect the residents and communities of Livingston County,” he said. He added that his background in municipal law prepared him for these responsibilities but acknowledged that serving as county attorney involves broader obligations: “The role of county attorney is both a legal advisor and a public servant,” said Lenahan. “The job is not just about addressing legal issues when they arise, but also helping the County make thoughtful, well-informed decisions that serve the public interest and further the interests of the County.”
Lenahan holds degrees from SUNY College at Fredonia (political science) and University of Pittsburgh School of Law (magna cum laude). He serves as president of Landmark Society of Western New York’s board of trustees, participates on youth sports boards, enjoys history, running, coaching youth sports with his wife, and spending time with their three children.
Founded in 1821, Livingston County is home to more than 61,000 residents across its 17 towns.
